Please independently adopt, run public tests, and review patch-1 (SpanSelector axes-limits fix).

Root cause: SpanSelector.new_axes() creates the span Rectangle at (0, 0) and adds it via `self.ax.add_patch(self._rect)`. Axes.add_patch -> _update_patch_limits registers the patch in ax.dataLim, so the invisible widget rectangle pulls 0 into the autoscaled xlim. `_setup_edge_handle` additionally builds ToolLineHandles at self.extents == (0, 0).

Fix (single line, lib/matplotlib/widgets.py SpanSelector.new_axes): `self.ax.add_patch(self._rect)` -> `self.ax.add_artist(self._rect)`. The rectangle is still drawn/rendered as an Axes artist, but it no longer contributes to data limits.

Verification I ran on this exact version (v2): `pytest lib/matplotlib/tests/test_widgets.py -k span` -> 4 collected, 4 passed, 0 failed (test_span_selector, test_span_selector_drag[True], test_span_selector_drag[False], test_span_selector_direction).

Independent check suggestion: `ax.plot([10,20],[10,20]); SpanSelector(ax, print, "horizontal", interactive=True)` then assert `ax.get_xlim()` is ~ (8.6, 21.4) and does not include 0.

Your localized note points at the ToolLineHandles at x=0; note those are created by axvline (Axes.add_line), which does NOT update dataLim in this version, so on its own it is not the trigger — the add_patch path is. Please confirm empirically with your own run.

Review status from member_002 (independent reviewer) — important, plus one disclosure.

SUBSTANTIVE VERDICT: patch-1 is CORRECT. I endorse the fix on real evidence.
- patch-1 changes exactly one product line: lib/matplotlib/widgets.py, SpanSelector.new_axes: `self.ax.add_patch(self._rect)` -> `self.ax.add_artist(self._rect)`. Confirmed via diff_workspace and patch-1's changed_paths (only widgets.py).
- Mechanism matches the issue: add_patch routes through _update_patch_limits and registers the invisible (0,0)-anchored Rectangle in ax.dataLim, pulling 0 into the autoscaled xlim. add_artist does not register data limits, so xlim stays at (10,20)+margins as expected.
- I wrote an independent regression test for the issue's exact repro (ax.plot([10,20],[10,20]); SpanSelector(..., interactive=True)) and got a verified same-version pass: 5 passed / 0 failed, with the 4 pre-existing SpanSelector tests also green.

PROCESS GAP: I could NOT file a formal accepted review record. org_review_patch requires an adoption record matching my CURRENT tree, and my tree no longer matches patch-1's content. Do not rely on my tree.

DISCLOSURE: I made a destructive mistake in my own private tree — a write_file replaced lib/matplotlib/tests/test_widgets.py with a placeholder, gutting that test module. My tree is damaged. This does NOT touch patch-1 (patch-1 changes only widgets.py), so your candidate is unaffected. I stopped reconstructing to avoid draining the shared budget (~277k tokens left).

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS FOR YOU (delivery owner): on your own intact tree, integrate_patch patch-1 -> run_tests on that exact version -> fix_patch(task_ids=[]) -> submit_integration. Your copy is clean; mine is not.
If you specifically need a formal accepted review record from me, publish a fresh fixed candidate and tell me; I can adopt it into a clean tree and test it. Be aware that costs real budget. I will not fabricate a pass or claim tests I did not run on the current version.
